slides.title: LineGuide
slides.footer: Hypothetical Scenario C proposal • Product not deployed
slides.notes: LineGuide is a hypothetical product proposal for Udacity Scenario C. Request: authorize only a two-week discovery stage, capped at USD 11,000, inside a conditional USD 65,000 ceiling for the full twelve-week plan. A later decision determines whether to fund the remaining stages. No customer interviews, model evaluations or production outcomes have been completed.

slides.title: Technicians struggle to find applicable answers
rows: Search English articles, compare manuals and parts, then escalate unresolved questions.
150 queries per day; 95% use mobile. Five languages are named in the scenario.
Search time, resolution rate, support cost and downtime loss are unknown.
slides.notes: Business problem: Technicians struggle to find the right answer in an English knowledgebase spanning many robot configurations. Unresolved searches consume their time and require company support. Scenario givens are hypothetical, supplied by the assignment. Users are aged 20 to 60; languages: English, Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Urdu. Device access 95% mobile 75% computer 25% tablet and education 85% high school 35% community college overlap and must not be added or normalized. Measure the search baseline in weeks 1 to 2.
slides.footer: Source: supplied hypothetical Scenario C; figures are not measured company data

slides.title: The product and its customer benefit
slides.statement: LineGuide explains approved reference material, cites its exact revision and retrieves verified parts for the selected robot configuration.
slides.body:
It asks for missing model or firmware details and prepares a technician-reviewed support handoff when evidence is missing or a request is hazardous.

Technicians gain a short explanation and an openable source for their machine.
slides.notes: Two-sentence solution: LineGuide is a mobile assistant that explains approved reference material in plain language, cites the exact source revision, and retrieves verified catalog records for the technician’s robot configuration. It asks for missing model or firmware details and sends unresolved or hazardous requests to established support channels with a technician-reviewed context bundle. Customer appeal depends on applicability, fast source access, short answers and honest uncertainty; wrong parts, translation errors and repeated configuration entry threaten adoption.
slides.footer: Proposed benefit; faster or safer outcomes have not been demonstrated

slides.title: Use an LLM where conversation helps
rows: Baseline; find exact terms and approved documents
Technician still interprets and reconciles results
Permissions, configuration, parts and prohibited actions
Clarify varied wording; explain retrieved passages
Can invent claims; needs constrained retrieval and review
slides.caption: Keep deterministic truth in records. Test the LLM’s added value against improved search.
slides.notes: No application-specific performance has been measured. RAG retrieves grounding material but does not guarantee correct answers or faithful citations. Fine-tuning is deferred: authoritative facts change and remain in retrievable records. Consider it later only for a repeatable behavior gap that prompt/retrieval changes cannot fix, with licensed redacted examples and held-out tests.

slides.title: System goals and first-release scope
slides.left:
Increase verified self-service resolution of eligible documentation and catalog questions.

Secondary goals
Reduce time to a verified answer.
Prevent unsupported or hazardous assistance.
slides.right:
Two models; up to 200 approved articles across five topics, subject to content audit.

Read-only explanations and catalog lookup.

Spanish follows its own validation; other languages remain staged.
slides.notes: Initial audience: authorized maintenance technicians reviewing reference information away from active hazardous work. English only at initial pilot. Later Spanish, Mandarin, written Cantonese and Urdu each need their own technical language validation; Cantonese must not be treated as Mandarin and Urdu needs right-to-left UI testing. Voice is outside the MVP. Pilot coverage is a proposed scope, not the actual distribution of source documents.
slides.footer: Proposed scope; document suitability and language performance are untested

slides.title: The technician’s path through the product
rows: Sign in, select robot and firmware, then ask a reference question.
Provide missing configuration before retrieval; keep that context visible on mobile.
Read a short explanation, exact catalog record and source link with revision.
Review the support context before sharing it; use the established safety route.
slides.notes: The mobile interface should have large tap targets, short readable answers, source links and an accessible escalation control. For procedural questions, open the complete approved procedure in the controlled original viewer, with prerequisites, warnings, revision and applicability. The LLM must not shorten, reorder or invent safety-critical steps. During outages, generate no new answers; show outage state and established support. Offline reference caching stays disabled until permission expiry, revocation, revision and deletion behavior is verified.
slides.footer: Proposed user flow • No robot commands, work authorization or part ordering

slides.title: RAG architecture and trust boundaries
slides.notes: Proposed components: responsive mobile web client; Microsoft Entra ID; API/orchestrator; policy and configuration checks; Azure AI Search hybrid index; Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry; approved manuals in Blob Storage; authoritative relational parts store; response validator; human support; privacy-filtered audit events. TLS protects device/API transport. Backend services use private endpoints where available, managed identities and least privilege. Derive tenant identity from the authenticated session, filter entitlements before retrieval and recheck before delivery. The API performs read-only catalog lookup. Validate citations, applicability and parts before displaying the response. No network route or credentials reach robot controllers. Audit request IDs, source revisions, model/prompt/index versions, policy outcome, timings and review disposition. Disable raw query logs by default.
slides.footer: Proposed architecture • External generation remains subject to approved regional/provider terms

slides.title: Approved content controls retrieval quality
rows: Preserve owner, revision, section, model, firmware, language and entitlement metadata.
Start near 500-token sections with 80-token overlap; hybrid top 20, rerank to at most five passages.
Confirm cited revisions and compatibility; exact-match every emitted part to permitted records.
Missing configuration, withdrawn content or incompatible parts trigger clarification or support.
slides.notes: These chunking and retrieval values are proposed starting settings. Keep warnings attached to their sections. Reject withdrawn records and missing approval or applicability metadata. The structured parts catalog is separate from document chunks; embeddings cannot establish part validity. Pin model, prompt, embedding and index versions together, and rehearse rollback. Cache only within tenant and permission scope. The embedding candidate is text-embedding-3-small; verify its current Azure region/version support and retrieval quality before use.
slides.footer: Starting retrieval settings; held-out evaluation decides whether to change them

slides.title: LLM deployment and configuration
rows: Azure OpenAI gpt-6-luna, 2026-09-22; benchmark before selection
Responses API; reasoning low; max_output_tokens 2,000 including reasoning
Retrieved context ≤8,000 tokens; visible answer target ≤800; 15-second deadline
Vendor default; test endpoint compatibility before overriding
Structured citations + escalation; no fine-tuning or autonomous tool loop
slides.notes: These are proposed settings, not tested optima. Candidate: Azure gpt-6-luna version 2026-09-22. Benchmark it and a stronger current model using the same frozen set; choose the smallest that passes every gate. Account entitlement, regional quota and lifecycle are unverified. Temperature is omitted because Microsoft R01 conflicts: its GPT-6 table marks it supported but the unsupported-parameters section excludes models other than Astra. Use vendor sampling defaults until endpoint testing resolves this. The 2,000-token output cap includes reasoning; target no more than 800 visible tokens. Incomplete output produces a safe excerpt or escalation, never an unvalidated partial answer. No fine-tuning, persistent conversation memory, external browsing or autonomous tool loop.
slides.footer: Candidate version is documented; account access, quality, latency and configuration are untested

slides.title: Security and privacy requirements
slides.left:
Derive tenant and groups on the server.

Filter before retrieval and recheck before delivery.

Treat retrieved text as untrusted; allow only read-only tools.

Encrypt transport and limit service privileges.
slides.right:
Select an approved regional or DataZone deployment.

Disable raw-query logs by default.

Review abuse-monitoring, retention and deletion terms before customer data enters the endpoint.
slides.caption: Azure’s no-training statement does not establish zero retention or safety certification.
slides.notes: Microsoft states prompts, completions, embeddings and training data are unavailable to OpenAI/other customers and are not used to train foundation models without permission/instruction. Abuse monitoring can include storage and authorized Microsoft human review; modified monitoring requires approval. Global deployments may process in any supported geography; DataZone remains within its specified zone. Do not claim unconditional single-region residency, zero retention, regulatory compliance or safety certification. Privacy/legal review and appropriate contracts precede proprietary data. Separate development and production. Test tenant leakage, injection, revocation and deletion.
slides.footer: Requirements before customer-data use; no compliance or certification claim

slides.title: Five risks and accountable mitigations
rows: Refuse live recovery or bypass; show complete procedures; critical escape suspends capability
Require configuration; filter current records; validate every emitted part; abstain on conflict
Enforce tenant access on server; minimize logs; test injection and cross-tenant isolation
Release each language separately; bilingual technical review; preserve warnings and identifiers
Benchmark search; short mobile answers; retain support; measure outcomes and full run cost
slides.notes: These are five product risks, not an exhaustive safety assessment. The service has no controller connection and cannot authorize physical work or order parts. Ambiguous hazardous requests receive escalation. Qualified personnel retain responsibility for physical work. A critical escape suspends the affected capability for safety review. Delaying experimentation preserves current search friction and escalation, but their monetary size is unknown. A bounded discovery stage tests whether an LLM adds enough value to justify its operating and review costs.

slides.title: Success measures: customer outcomes
rows: Confirmed correct resolution, no escalation within 24 h / all eligible sessions; ≥70%
Median time to correct answer or appropriate escalation; ≥30% lower than search
slides.caption: Abstentions, missing feedback and escalations remain in the resolution denominator.
slides.notes: Resolution numerator: eligible sessions with technician-confirmed resolution, domain-review confirmation and no support escalation within 24 hours. Denominator: all eligible sessions, including abstentions, missing feedback and escalations. Use the same eligibility for search. For task time, 25 technicians complete 16 trials each, eight search and eight assistant, using distinct matched variants and counterbalanced order. This yields 200 trials per condition. Report paired differences and uncertainty alongside completion and escalation rates. This pilot screen does not prove population-wide lift. Report every KPI by enabled language and robot model. All targets are proposed and unmeasured.
slides.footer: Two of five proposed measurements • Baselines and outcomes are not yet measured

slides.title: Success measures: quality and reliability
rows: ≥98% correctness; 0 wrong parts; ≥76/80 known record returns; 20/20 ambiguous clarifications
≥200 substantive answers; domain review; abstentions fail known cases
0 observed escapes / 100 prohibited cases per language
Any critical escape suspends affected capability
≤8 seconds; failures and timeouts exceed target
slides.caption: Zero observed safety escapes in curated tests does not certify industrial safety.
slides.notes: Correctness numerator: substantive answers whose material claims have applicable current cited support and whose emitted parts exactly match compatible permitted catalog records. Denominator: all substantive answered cases. Require at least 200 substantive answers and at least 98% correctness. The 100 catalog cases contain 80 unique known parts and 20 ambiguous or unknown cases. Require at least 76/80 correct record returns, 20/20 appropriate clarifications or escalations, and zero wrong part emissions. Abstentions count as failed known-record returns. Safety escape rate is actionable prohibited assistance divided by all prohibited requests. Require zero observed escapes in 100 cases per language and no critical escape in supervised use. Zero of 100 would imply an approximate 3% upper 95% bound only with independent representative sampling; curated tests do not meet that assumption or certify safety. Latency is empirical p95 from server acceptance to fully validated response or abstention; failures and timeouts exceed the target. Use 500 requests at 10 concurrency and record query mix, cache state and versions.
slides.footer: Three of five proposed measurements • No model result or load test has been observed

slides.title: Validation before supervised use
rows: 400 disjoint items: 200 routine, 100 catalog and 100 prohibited requests.
Domain reviewers score support, applicability and parts; safety lead adjudicates escapes.
Test isolation, injection, missing evidence, outages, expiry and rollback; no unvalidated streaming.
Use matched search/assistant tasks; review all supervised sessions and full operating cost.
slides.notes: The English release set has 400 disjoint semantic cases: 200 routine, 100 catalog and 100 prohibited requests. The catalog split is 80 unique known records and 20 ambiguous or unknown cases, with the subgates on slide 14. These are proposed tests, not executed results. Customer tasks and catalogs are unavailable; qualified reviewers must create and approve them. Freeze the release set before tuning. The separate 500 request load test uses a pinned deployment. Test 1,500 requests/day before claiming tenfold headroom over the scenario 150 daily. Block delivery until validation completes. Each later language repeats its own semantic and safety validation. An LLM cannot be the sole grader of itself.
slides.footer: Proposed acceptance plan • Tests and customer studies remain to be run

slides.title: Illustrative monthly capacity value
slides.statement: 970.2 successful assisted sessions × 5 minutes saved × $40/hour ≈ $3,234 per month
slides.body:
150 queries/day × 22 days × 60% eligible × 70% adoption × 70% verified resolution = 970.2 sessions.

Assume $1,600/month run cost: $800 cloud allowance  + 16 review hours at $50. Base net capacity value: $1,634/month before implementation.
slides.notes: Currency: USD. Only 150 queries/day is supplied by the scenario. The 22 service days, eligibility 60%, adoption 70%, resolution 70%, five minutes saved and $40/hour are assumptions. Exact calculation: 150*22*.6*.7*.7= 970.2; 970.2*5/60*40=3234. Recurring cost 800 + 16*50=1600; base net 1634. The $800 cloud/search/storage/model allowance is not a vendor quote and must be replaced with a confirmed Azure estimate. This is redeployable staff capacity, not cash savings, avoided downtime, revenue or a forecast. A query is not a unique technician. Do not add support/downtime benefits without separate measurement and overlap checks.
slides.footer: Illustrative assumptions in USD • No measured savings or vendor quotation

slides.title: Sensitivity and investment discipline
slides.caption: Base recurring break-even: 2.47 minutes saved/session. $60,000 labor payback: 36.7 months.
slides.notes: All cases use 150 queries/day, 22 days/month and USD 40/hour. Conservative assumptions: 40% eligible, 50% adoption, 60% resolution, three minutes saved. Base: 60%, 70%, 70%, five minutes. Favorable: 80%, 85%, 80%, seven minutes. Monthly run cost is assumed USD 1,600 in all cases. Base recurring break-even: 1600/970.2/40*60=2.47371676 minutes. Simple labor-only implementation payback: 60000/1634=36.7197 months, excluding pilot run allowance, financing and ramp effects. This weak standalone case does not justify committing the full pilot now. Discovery must establish measured demand, task time, source coverage, current quotations and the sponsor investment hurdle; otherwise stop or improve search alone. Capacity creates value only if it can be redeployed.
slides.footer: Scenarios are sensitivity cases; ranges are not statistical confidence intervals

slides.title: Twelve-week pilot and stakeholder decision
rows: Audit sources and search baseline; measure demand and task time before a further funding decision.
If discovery supports investment, build read-only RAG, catalog checks and audit events.
Complete independent tests, then supervised English use if gates pass.
Choose stop, revise or expand using all five measures and observed economics.
slides.caption: Ask: authorize only $11,000 discovery now; remaining stages conditional within a $65,000 ceiling.
slides.notes: Authorize only the first two weeks now: at most USD 10,000 labor plus USD 1,000 run and independent-review allowance. This USD 11,000 cap is included in the conditional total USD 65,000 ceiling. If all stages proceed, staffing is one application engineer, one ML/retrieval engineer, 0.25 FTE domain expert and 0.25 FTE PM/designer for twelve weeks: 30 person-weeks at USD 2,000 = USD 60,000. Three months recurring allowance adds USD 4,800, giving USD 64,800. Independent quality review is outside the 30 person-weeks. Existing safety/security reviewers must fit the envelope; otherwise re-scope. Reconcile actual discovery spend before releasing more funding. Weeks 6 to 8 cover independent quality, isolation, injection, accessibility, load and rollback tests; weeks 9 to 10 are supervised English use away from active hazardous work. Spanish needs separate bilingual validation. The sponsor should assign domain and safety reviewers and authorize approved sources in the selected region. No funding, source access or production approval is asserted.
slides.footer: Proposed budget and authorization request • No funding or production approval asserted
